focuses.expected_description: Socialist ministers must establish civilian responsibility without treating every officer as a political opponent. A professional civilian defence ministry will clarify command and move routine administration out of the uniformed establishment.

focuses.expected_description: A negotiated service compact can secure professional cooperation while the government carries out its social programme. Protecting military careers will improve command confidence but preserve a more expensive officer establishment.

focuses.expected_description: Every department should purchase through public rules rather than through the networks inherited with its offices. Competitive procurement will strengthen services and reduce the waste that can discredit an ambitious social government.

focuses.expected_description: The Socialist programme now joins a chosen industrial settlement to funded public institutions and civilian responsibility. A settled administration will make these commitments dependable beyond the first years of reform.

focuses.expected_description: A planned economy needs its own machinery and engineering capacity rather than a larger list of targets. A Basque industrial complex will place productive assets behind the public investment programme.

focuses.expected_description: Workplace ownership needs technical knowledge that cannot remain the privilege of a few large firms. Cooperative institutes will spread industrial methods and help elected boards judge the advice they receive.

focuses.expected_description: Public support and worker participation should return part of rising enterprise income to society. A defined public dividend will strengthen revenue without allowing ministries to substitute opaque levies for published accounts.

focuses.expected_description: The left's neighbourhood organizations confront housing and service problems that industrial ministries cannot settle. Giving municipal administrations trained staff will improve local services while keeping their accounts open to public scrutiny.

focuses.expected_description: Madrid's working districts need professional employment and public institutions alongside factories and crowded housing. A local service centre will put the municipal programme on a more durable economic footing.
